title: Controller Policy Results
comparison_safety_rules: Compared modes must use the same workload timeline and request population.
The active Scenario 1 protocol forbids application-level priority classes; numeric backend ranks may only be derived from replay-ready time.
Controller capabilities must be isolated unless the record explicitly names a combination.
A valid result requires trace coverage and no client-side replay-dispatch delay dominating the outcome.

experiments.question: Can expected tool-return times improve replay scheduling when no task is designated more important by the front end?
experiments.controller_capability: Ready-time ordering and safe GPU backfill only; backend priority numbers are temporary queue ranks derived by the controller.
experiments.priority_contract: All 16 sessions have equal application importance. Both former target-role and filler-role replays have deadlines. No front-end priority, QoS tier, urgent label, or demotable background class is allowed.
experiments.workload: DeepAgents; P3; 16 sessions x 2 replay steps = 32 deadline-bearing replays per mode; identical seeded workload shape.

parameters.instrumentation: strict live preflight; 32/32 replay timing samples and queue-rank linkage required

results.replay_coverage: 32/32 requests per mode, including both workload-generation roles
results.mechanism_proof: No front-end priority signal; all non-sentinel requests were peer/normal, and RTG derived a backend queue rank for every replay.

experiments.question: Does the equal-importance controller experiment still run and pass the shared instrumentation gate?
experiments.controller_capability: Ready-time ordering and GPU backfill only; the front end supplies no importance class.
experiments.priority_contract: All 16 sessions have equal application importance; both workload roles have replay deadlines. The controller alone derives backend queue ranks.
experiments.workload: DeepAgents; P3; 16 sessions x 2 replay steps = 32 deadline-bearing replays per mode; identical seeded workload shape.

parameters.instrumentation: strict static and live preflights; shared controller_queue gate passed in both cases; 45 adapter hooks inventoried

results.replay_coverage: 32/32 requests per mode, including both workload-generation roles
results.mechanism_proof: No front-end priority in either mode; strict preflight and shared controller_queue evidence gate passed for both cases.

experiments.question: Can early replay-ready-time knowledge improve scheduling for equal-importance replay requests?
experiments.controller_capability: Ready-time scheduling only; GPU-idle telemetry was observed but did not alter admission in this reference run.
experiments.priority_contract: Historical run predating the enforced equal-importance contract. Its target/filler metadata must not be assumed equivalent to the active Scenario 1 protocol.
experiments.workload: Hatcher; P3; 16 replay-capable sessions x 2 replay steps = 32 replays per mode; 15 concurrent peer sessions; mode-independent timeline.

results.mechanism_proof: 32/32 controller replays received ready-time ordering at the local gate and SGLang boundary.

experiments.reproduction_command: Historical evidence only; use the active equal-importance Scenario 1 entry for new runs.

experiments.question: Can the controller prepare useful KV during long tool waits without fake warmup requests?
experiments.controller_capability: Direct KV preparation with selective admission only.
experiments.priority_contract: All replay requests have equal application importance. Admission depends on safe completion and expected reuse, not user-priority class.
experiments.workload: Hatcher; P3; 32 replay requests per mode; long tool waits only; mode-independent timeline.

results.mechanism_proof: 21/21 controller preparation requests reached the backend; 9 needed load plans and 12 were already resident.

experiments.reproduction_command: Use the recorded run configuration in the linked artifact before creating a new Scenario 2 spec; do not combine it with scheduling or eviction.

experiments.question: Can harness-derived prefix value guide native priority-radix eviction?
experiments.priority_contract: Application value classes are intentionally present: high, normal, and low prefixes map to 100, 0, and -100. This is not comparable to an equal-importance scheduling experiment.
experiments.workload: Hatcher; P3; 32 replay requests per mode; mode-independent timeline.

parameters.tool_wait_profile: very short through long, using the Scenario 1 distribution

results.tradeoff: Overall workload window increased by 63.1 s.
results.mechanism_proof: 0 priority mismatches; native priority-radix eviction was active.

experiments.reproduction_command: Use the recorded run configuration in the linked artifact before creating a new Scenario 3 spec; do not combine it with scheduling or direct KV preparation.

experiments.question: Did the modularity restructuring preserve the original Scenario 1 behavior?
experiments.priority_contract: Historical run predating the enforced equal-importance contract; do not compare it as if it used the active request metadata.
experiments.workload: Exact Scenario 1 reference workload and seed.

results.verdict: Clean aggregate win: replay TTFT, replay deadline debt, and full workload duration all improved.
